blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
There are two basic ways to decide when to record a transaction. Cash accounting records it the day the money actually moves — when you pay, or when you are paid. It is simple and easy.

But cash accounting misses things. A big sale in December that the customer pays in January is invisible in December. Accrual accounting is different: it records the transaction when it happens, not when the money moves. So the December sale is in the December accounts, even if the payment arrives later.

Most real companies use accrual accounting, because it shows the true shape of the business month by month.

items.q: When does cash accounting record a transaction?
options: The day the sale is agreed
At the end of the year
When the customer signs the contract
items.why: "Cash accounting records it the day the money actually moves."

items.q: Where is the December sale in accrual accounting?
items.why: "the December sale is in the December accounts, even if the payment arrives later."

items.q: Why do most real companies use accrual accounting?
options: It shows the true shape of the business month by month
items.why: "it shows the true shape of the business month by month."

items.q: The text suggests that cash accounting can…
options: hide a real sale for a month
items.why: Inferência: a venda de dezembro fica "invisible" até o pagamento chegar em janeiro.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Accrual gives a clearer monthly picture
Cash accounting always shows the true shape of the business
A late payment can hide a sale in cash accounting
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o caixa esconde coisas; só o accrual mostra a forma real.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicando ao novo colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, welcome to the team. You asked a good question. You looked at the December report and you saw a big sale. But the customer has not paid yet. They will pay in January. So why is it already in December?

The answer is easy. We use accrual accounting here. Accrual means we record the sale when it happens, not when the money arrives. The sale happened in December, so it goes in December. The payment comes later, and that is fine.

If we used cash accounting, we would wait for the money. The sale would be invisible until January. December would look weak, and January would look very strong. But that is not the true shape of the business.

At Czarnikow, timing matters a lot. We trade all the time, and very often the money moves much later. So accrual shows us the real picture, month by month, and we can trust the numbers. When you read any report, always check the method first. Is it cash or is it accrual? It changes everything. Once you know the method, the numbers make sense.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is the sale already in the December report?
options: The sale happened in December and they use accrual accounting
items.why: "We use accrual accounting… the sale happened in December, so it goes in December."

items.q: When will the customer pay?
options: At the end of the year
items.why: "They will pay in January."

items.q: What would happen with cash accounting?
options: The sale would be invisible until January
The sale would stay in December
items.why: "The sale would be invisible until January."

items.q: Sophie suggests that, with cash accounting, December would…
options: look weak and January look strong
look strong and January look weak
show no sales at all for the year
items.why: Inferência: sem a venda, dezembro fica fraco e janeiro fica muito forte.

items.q: Why does Sophie say you should check the method first?
options: Because it is a company rule
Because the method changes how the numbers look
items.why: Inferência: "It changes everything" — o método muda a leitura do relatório.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We record the sale in December." To record means to…
items.why: To record = registrar, anotar nas contas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "With cash accounting, we wait until the money ___."
items.why: "the day the money actually moves" — o caixa espera o dinheiro se mover.

items.q: "The December sale is invisible in the cash report." Invisible means…
items.why: Invisible = invisível, não aparece no relatório.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Accrual shows the ___ of the business, month by month."
items.why: "it shows the true shape of the business" — a forma real do negócio.

items.q: "Accrual accounting records the sale when it happens." This means it records the sale…
options: at the moment the sale happens, not when money moves
items.why: Accrual (competência) registra pelo fato gerador, não pelo caixa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre contas e relatórios. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the December report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new method next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = colocar em uso, implementar.

items.q: "The customer is late, so the payment is overdue." Overdue means…
items.why: Overdue = atrasado, passou do prazo.

items.q: "Cash and accrual can add up to a very different profit." To add up means to…
items.why: Add up = somar, chegar a um total.

items.q: "Please write down the date of each sale." To write down means to…
options: note it on paper or in a system
items.why: Write down = anotar, registrar por escrito.
